condition: VTE risk and thromboprophylaxis — major pelvic cancer surgery (Caprini 11)
summary: 68-year-old woman, BMI 33, previous provoked DVT, varicose veins, for laparoscopic anterior resection of rectal cancer — Caprini 11 (high risk).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Pre-operative planning for rectal cancer operation
inputs.hpi: Upper rectal adenocarcinoma (cT3N0M0) after MDT discussion; listed for laparoscopic anterior resection in 2 weeks. Left leg DVT in 2015 after a knee arthroscopy, treated for 3 months. Varicose veins. No bleeding disorder. Mobile and independent.

exam.general: Well. HR 74, BP 138/82, RR 14, SpO2 98% on air, T 36.6°C. BMI 33.

imaging.result: Upper rectal tumour at 12 cm, T3b, N0, CRM clear, EMVI negative.

guideline.name: NICE NG89 — Venous thromboembolism in over 16s: reducing the risk of hospital-acquired DVT or PE
guideline.section: Assess VTE and bleeding risk; abdominal surgery with VTE risk above bleeding risk: pharmacological prophylaxis (LMWH) for at least 7 days; extended to 28 days after major cancer surgery in the abdomen/pelvis; mechanical prophylaxis (anti-embolism stockings or IPC) when pharmacological prophylaxis is contraindicated by bleeding risk; reassess within 24 h and when the clinical situation changes
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. VTE in over 16s (NG89). London: NICE; 2018 (updated 2019).

guideline.name: ACCP 9th edition — prevention of VTE in non-orthopaedic surgical patients (Caprini)
guideline.section: General and abdominal-pelvic surgery: Caprini ≥5 high risk → LMWH/LDUH plus mechanical prophylaxis; extended-duration (4 weeks) LMWH after abdominal/pelvic cancer surgery; high bleeding risk → mechanical prophylaxis until bleeding risk diminishes
guideline.citation: Gould MK, Garcia DA, Wren SM, et al. Chest. 2012;141(2 Suppl):e227S–77S.

rationale: Base VTE case: very high VTE risk, low bleeding risk. Tests Caprini suggestion, pharmacological prophylaxis, extended 28-day prophylaxis and mechanical prophylaxis.
